status_meaning: The proposed text these vectors test is immature. This is an ordinary lab-authored fixture, not a docs/CANDIDATES.md submission.
description: Resources designated inside invocation arguments (the confused deputy). A synthetic boundary in front of a synthetic tool registry decides whether every resource operand a call designates is authorized by the credential the caller selected for that operand, separately from service-owned effects that run under a declared service credential. Admitted calls run against an in-memory store with an access trace. Every vector is candidate against proposed text. draft-pidlisnyi-aps-04 states no such rule. See README.
evaluation: Each presentation is an independent evaluation against a fresh copy of initial_store. No state is carried between presentations and presentation order does not matter.
assumptions: The requester is an assumed authenticated identity.
Tool contracts are trusted and honest: each tool performs exactly the accesses its program in README "Tools" lists. Dishonest or stale contracts are outside v0.
Credentials and issuer records are trusted fixture-side state. A call names credentials by identifier only.
Resolution is lexical and pinned. The boundary and the tool resolve through the same function and nothing changes between admission and execution.

target-binding.role: motivating concept, not the rule under test
target-binding.section: Lifecycle concepts are separate > Authority and dependencies
target-binding.quote: Target binding. Which resource, counterparty or object the authority applies to. Continuity of a name does not by itself establish continuity of the thing named.

draft04_counterpart.quote: Target binding Which resource, counterparty or object the authority applies to. Continuity of a name does not on its own establish continuity of the thing named.

csr-operands.quote: For this family's caller-supplied-resource profile, the boundary identifies every resource operand that the trusted tool contract says will be accessed, and the operation required on that operand.

csr-selected-authority.quote: It authorizes each operand using authority explicitly selected for that operand in this invocation. It does not substitute ambient service credentials or other credentials held by the requester.

csr-closed-arguments.quote: Supplied arguments the contract does not classify are refused under this profile, and so is a call that omits an operand the contract requires.

csr-service-effects.quote: Any service-owned effect uses a separately declared authority source and cannot be redirected by that exception to a resource the caller selects.

csr-holder-bound-credentials.quote: Under this profile a credential is resolved against trusted state, must be held by the authenticated requester, and must chain to an issuer the trusted issuer records give standing over the resource. A delegated credential needs a delegable parent held by its issuer and may be equal to that parent but no wider.

csr-exact-call.quote: When a decision is presented, the boundary admits only the exact call the decision names, including its authority selections.
csr-exact-call.status: proposed in README.md, an analogue of draft-pidlisnyi-aps-04 section 9.2 over this family's own call reference

target.quote: target is the exact resource, tool, or endpoint against which the action will be dispatched; a profile MUST define its target string construction.

exact_call.quote: At the next authorization boundary the boundary MUST compare the call it is about to admit against the action the approval names, and MUST NOT admit a call whose action reference differs from it. An argument changed after the decision produces a different action reference, so the comparison catches it without any separate argument-level rule.

exact_call_non_establishment.quote: It does not establish that the arguments mean what the requesting agent intended them to mean.

identifiers.covering_rule: A credential over canonical identifier E covers canonical identifier R when R equals E or R begins with E followed by /.

call_ref.note: This family's own call reference over its own call object {tool, requester, arguments, authority}. It is not an APS action_ref.

defective_policies.name: no-call-binding
defective_policies.change: A presented decision is not compared with the call.

defective_policies.name: leaf-walk
defective_policies.change: Undeclared-path refusal and designation see only non-container values, as in revision 0.1. An empty container is invisible, and a declared operand holding one yields no designation.

defective_policies.name: open-schema
defective_policies.change: An argument path the contract does not declare is ignored instead of refused.

defective_policies.name: no-required-check
defective_policies.change: Required operands are not checked for presence.

defective_policies.name: target-only
defective_policies.change: Only the operand at the contract's target path is a designation. Validation, binding and service effects are unchanged.

defective_policies.name: shallow-args
defective_policies.change: Only top-level operands are designations. An operand inside an object or an array is not.

defective_policies.name: shape-guessing
defective_policies.change: A declared node holding a string that begins with res: in any case is a resource designation, with the contract's operation for a resource operand and read for data. A resource operand holding anything else is not a designation. Capability operands are unchanged.

defective_policies.name: dedup-by-resource
defective_policies.change: After resolution, a designation whose resource was already designated earlier in the walk is skipped.

defective_policies.name: no-canonicalization
defective_policies.change: Coverage compares the raw designation string with the same covering rule. The tool still resolves canonically.

defective_policies.name: wallet-search
defective_policies.change: When the selected credential fails for a name-form operand, any credential the requester holds in trusted state that passes C and K is used instead.

defective_policies.name: pooled-selection
defective_policies.change: When the selected credential fails for a name-form operand, any credential selected anywhere in the call that passes C and K is used instead.

defective_policies.name: deputy-authority
defective_policies.change: When the selected credential fails for a name-form operand, any credential held by the tool's service identity that passes C and K for that identity is used instead.

defective_policies.name: holder-unchecked
defective_policies.change: The credential's holder is not compared with the requester.

defective_policies.name: self-asserted-issuer
defective_policies.change: A root credential's issuer is accepted without consulting the trusted issuer records.

defective_policies.name: delegation-equals-exercise
defective_policies.change: A parent credential's delegable flag is ignored, so holding an exercise right is treated as permission to delegate it.

defective_policies.name: no-attenuation-check
defective_policies.change: A delegated credential is not compared with its parent's resource and operations.

defective_policies.name: strict-attenuation
defective_policies.change: A delegated credential must be strictly narrower than its parent, so an equal delegation is refused.

defective_policies.name: resource-not-operation
defective_policies.change: Coverage checks the resource and ignores the operation. Attenuation along the chain is unchanged.

defective_policies.name: caller-authority-for-service-effects
defective_policies.change: A service-owned effect needs a credential the caller selects for it, which is revision 0.1's rule that service authority is never used. No call selects one.

presentations.note: Control. Alice selects her r1 read credential for src and her r2 write credential for dst, and a decision naming this exact call is presented. The copy runs.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-01: Alice holds only an r1 read and write credential and selects it for both operands. No decision is presented.
presentations.note: The call target (src) is covered. Only the destination named inside an argument is not.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-02: the service identity also holds cred:svc-r2-write. Alice's credentials and selection are unchanged.
presentations.note: The name-based confused deputy (Hardy 1988). The service could write r2 under its own credential, and a boundary that lets the service's credentials stand in for the caller's admits the call.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-02: the uncovered destination is two levels deep, at options.output.path, next to a data sibling options.output.format.
presentations.note: export reads src and writes the resource named at options.output.path. Alice has only an r1 read credential and selects it for both.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-04: Alice also holds an r2 write credential and selects it for options.output.path.
presentations.note: Positive control for nesting. The export writes csv:alpha into r2.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-04b: the destination is supplied under one literal top-level key "options.output.path" instead of nested objects.
presentations.note: An argument key must match [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, so a path string can never be read two ways. The refusal names the key in bracket-quoted form.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-02: the destinations are an array. dsts[0] is covered, dsts[1] is r3 and Alice selects her r2 credential for it.
presentations.note: replicate writes every element of dsts. The refusal names the exact index, and the covered r2 is not written either, because nothing runs before full admission.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-05: Alice also holds an r3 write credential and selects it for dsts[1].
presentations.note: Positive control for arrays. Both destinations receive alpha.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-05b: the fixture injects a failure at the dsts[1] write.
presentations.note: Admission is unchanged. Execution stops at dsts[1] and is reported as partial. The r2 write already done is kept and nothing is rolled back. The profile governs authority, not atomicity.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-01: a label argument carries the string res:/store/r3, over which Alice holds nothing. No decision is presented.
presentations.note: The contract declares label as data. Designation comes from the contract, not from what a string looks like, and the tool never touches r3.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-09: Alice selects an r2 write credential, and the content written is the string res:/store/r3.
presentations.note: By value. overwrite writes the characters res:/store/r3 into r2. It needs authority over r2 only, and r3 is never read.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-06b: the same identifier is passed by reference, as the src of a copy into r2. Alice holds only her r2 write credential and selects it for both operands.
presentations.note: By reference. copy reads r3, so it needs read authority over r3, which Alice does not have.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-01: the call carries an argument, compression, that the copy contract does not mention. No decision is presented.
presentations.note: Closed-argument profile. The value does not look like a resource and the tool would ignore it. The profile refuses it anyway, because the boundary cannot know what an unclassified argument does.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-07: the undeclared argument is extra, holding an empty object.
presentations.note: An empty container is still a supplied argument. A walk that visits only leaves never sees it.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-01: dst is absent. No decision is presented.
presentations.note: The contract declares dst as required. A call that omits it is refused before any designation is checked.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-01: dst holds an empty object instead of an identifier. No decision is presented.
presentations.note: A declared resource operand is a node, whatever its value. An object there has no identifier.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-02: dst is spelled res:/store/r1/../r2, which begins with the covered res:/store/r1/ and resolves to res:/store/r2.
presentations.note: Coverage is decided on the resolved identifier, the same one the tool writes. A raw prefix comparison reads it as beneath r1.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-01: dst is spelled RES:/Store/R2, a cased spelling of the covered res:/store/r2. No decision is presented.
presentations.note: Resolution works in both directions. A boundary that refuses every non-canonical spelling passes ADR-08 and fails this one.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-08: dst is res:/store/../../r2, whose second .. has no segment left to remove.
presentations.note: The designation has no canonical identifier, so it is refused as invalid before any credential is consulted.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-06b: Alice holds and selects only an r2 read credential.
presentations.note: The credential names the resource. It does not carry the operation the tool performs on it. Read and write are disjoint toy rights.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-01: dst carries a capability reference to cred:alice-r2-write instead of a name, so designation and authority arrive together.
presentations.note: Capability form. The designated resource is the credential's own. The credential is resolved against trusted state, is held by Alice and is issued by the owner of res:/store.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-10: the capability is cred:mallory-r2-write, held by party:mallory.
presentations.note: Holder-bound profile only. A capability passed along by its holder is not Alice's authority here. This says nothing about bearer tokens, which this profile does not model.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-10: the capability is delegated by party:bob from a parent over res:/store/r2/drafts only, and asserts all of res:/store/r2.
presentations.note: The write to r2 lies outside the parent's authority, so it is refused whether the over-broad child is rejected outright, as here, or intersected with its parent.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-10: the capability is cred:alice-r2-read, and the tool writes dst.
presentations.note: The capability-form counterpart of ADR-09.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-10: the capability is delegated by party:bob, whose delegable parent covers exactly r2 write, the same as the child.
presentations.note: Non-amplification permits equality. A child no wider than its parent is valid even when it is not narrower.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-10e: party:bob's parent covers r2 write but is not delegable.
presentations.note: Holding an exercise right does not grant a delegation right. Bob could write r2 himself and still cannot pass that on.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-10: the capability is a root credential issued by party:mallory, which the trusted issuer records do not list as owning anything under res:/store.
presentations.note: Issuer standing comes from trusted fixture-side records, not from what the credential says about itself.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-11b: the decision names copy(src=r1, dst=r2), and the presented call has dst=r3 with Alice's r3 write credential selected for it.
presentations.note: Both destinations are fully authorized, so scope checking cannot mask the binding check. The call is refused only because it is not the call the decision named.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-11: the presented call is the decided call.
presentations.note: Unchanged-call control with the same trusted state as ADR-11.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-12b: Alice holds both an r2 read and an r2 write credential and selects the read one for dst.
presentations.note: Holding authority is weaker than selecting it. The boundary evaluates only the credential selected for the operand and does not search Alice's other credentials.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-12: Alice selects her r2 write credential for dst.
presentations.note: Explicit-selection positive control.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-12: Alice selects nothing for dst.
presentations.note: An operand with no selected authority is refused even though Alice holds a credential that would cover it.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-13b: the two selections are swapped, so the stronger delegated read and write credential sits on src and the read-only root credential sits on dst.
presentations.note: normalize(src=r2, dst=r2) designates r2 twice with different operations. Each occurrence is checked against its own selection. The stronger credential selected for src does not stand in for dst.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-13: src selects the root r2 read credential and dst selects the r2 read and write credential delegated by party:bob.
presentations.note: Positive control. Two authority sources, one per occurrence. normalize upper-cases r2 in place.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-13b: Alice holds only an r2 write credential and selects it for both occurrences.
presentations.note: dst is covered for write. src is not covered for read. The read must not disappear because r2 was already checked once for another operation.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-01: the tool is copy_audited, whose contract declares a service-owned write to res:/svc/stats under cred:svc-stats-write.
presentations.note: Hardy's statistics file. Caller data moves under Alice's selected credentials, and the service records the copy in its own fixed resource under its own declared credential.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-14: dst is res:/svc/bill, inside the service's own home, and Alice selects her r2 write credential for it.
presentations.note: Hardy's billing file. The service could write there under cred:svc-home, but the caller chose this destination and holds no authority over it.

presentations.differs_from: ADR-14: dst is the service's statistics resource and Alice selects the service-effect credential cred:svc-stats-write for it.
presentations.note: The service-owned exception cannot be redirected. The declared service credential authorizes the service's fixed effect, and a caller cannot select it for an operand of its own.
